content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble installing [product_name] on a VMware virtual machine running Windows 7 32-bit. I downloaded the installer from [url], and I have my older [product_name] (version [version_no]) DVD in the drive. However, the setup fails during the check for a previous version and displays a message: 'No qualified version found.' Any suggestions?

Hello, The update server was temporarily unavailable. Try these steps: Insert your [product_name] [version_no] DVD. There should be a 'windows/tools' folder containing a file named [product_name].exe. Run this file, possibly in compatibility mode. If [product_name] [version_no] starts, use the update center to proceed with the update (several steps involved). The issue is that the update only works if a valid installation already exists on your PC; the DVD is not accepted for upgrading. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered an installation issue with [product_name] on a virtual machine using Windows 7 (32-bit). The installer fails during the verification of an existing qualified version and displays an error about no valid version being found. This highlights a common problem where upgrade processes require an installed previous version rather than accepting a DVD as proof of license.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to be able to install and upgrade the software using the previous version's DVD as proof of license, without needing an older installation to be already present on the system.
